Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 OBJECTIVE 2 SETUP 3 GAMEPLAY 4 COMBAT & DEFENSE 5 END OF GAME OBJECTIVE Defeat your opponent in this arcade-style fighting game by reducing their health to 0 . SETUP Each player chooses a Hero and their corresponding Action deck . Starting health is set to 25 . Each player draws 7 cards for their starting hand. The player who says "Ready, Fight!" first goes first. GAMEPLAY Players take turns performing actions. A turn consists of three phases: 1. Draw Phase: Draw 2 cards from your Action deck. (There is no hand limit). 2. Action Phase: You may play any number of cards to perform Attacks or activate effects. Joysticks: Cards representing movement or positioning. Buttons: Cards representing punches, kicks, or special moves. Combos: Combine cards according to the symbols on your Hero card to trigger extra effects or damage. 3. End Phase: Effects that last "until the end of the turn" expire. Play passes to the opponent. COMBAT & DEFENSE Attacking: The active player plays attack cards. Total damage is calculated. Defending: The defender can play Block cards (to reduce damage from Buttons) or Counter cards (to react to specific maneuvers). Star Power: You gain Star tokens through attacks and effects. Once you reach 5 tokens, your powerful Star Power Ability triggers automatically. Shields: Shield tokens can be spent to block incoming damage on a one-for-one basis. END OF GAME The game ends immediately when a player's health reaches 0 . The surviving player is the winner. [Rating: 3/10] I wanted to like this but pff, just too few meaningful decisions. I'd have like more deck cycling/ draw mitigation. The built-in combo system also rewards slow play with plenty of resting, where it would've been more interesting if the game pushed you to be a tad more reckless imo.

[Rating: 4/10] Initial Impressions: I love dueling games, but in this one it felt like the combos were very obvious and there wasn't really much room for clever play. And since moves seem obvious and you are just slugging damage back and forth then it doesn't feel like you are leveraging your character's power to play that differently.

[Rating: 6/10] Provisional rating. [EDIT: I sold the game because I lacked interest to play it again, so it becomes now my permanent rating.]  It falls in the same space as Combo Fighter and Pocket Paragons (both games I play solo, just like this one), and so far, I prefer both over Neon Reign.

[Rating: 6/10] This is okay - I was a bit disappointed though.  It was supposed to be some sort of videogame fighter experience, and it really is just about collecting and playing different sets to activate bonuses.  I wish the theme had been better developed and more prominent.  Still, it is travel friendly and the rules aren't super complex.  The solo is okay as well.
